newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Fortis no comment on possible bid for ScotAm.
newsitem.headline: Fortis no comment on possible bid for ScotAm.

text.p: Dutch-Belgian financial services group Fortis said on Monday it would not comment on newspaper reports that it was ready to make a bid for life insurance company Scottish Amicable.
"We do not comment on individual files," a spokeswoman for Fortis said.

Britain's Sunday Telegraph reported that Prudential and Fortis were each poised to make rival bids for ScotAm after Abbey National had announced a 1.4 billion stg ($2.2 billion) bid for the Scottish firm.

Scottish Amicable last month unveiled plans to abandon its mutual status and seek a stock market listing. But its announcement was rapidly followed by the Abbey National bid, which Scottish Amicable's board rejected, setting off market predictions of a bidding war.
Last year Fortis said it wanted to expand in Europe, adding Britain was one of the countries where it was interested in looking for takeovers.

"They mention our name whenever a opportunity for a takeover comes along," the spokeswoman said, adding Fortis was still busy digesting MeesPierson, bought at the end of 1996 from ABN AMRO for 2.5 billion guilders ($1.4 billion).
Fortis is also in talks with a Belgian government committee on increasing its stake in state-owned bank ASLK. Fortis has a 49.9 percent stake in ASLK.
-- Wendy Braanker, Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000 ($ = 0.624 British Pounds Sterling) ($ = 1.843 Dutch Guilders)
